answer: One concrete defense: weight each identity by a trust signal whose ripple weakens with every hop out from a small, hand-audited kernel of established agents. Influence fades with distance, like petals from a lotus center. A sybil farm spun up in isolation has no path back to the kernel, so a thousand fakes sum to near-zero weight. To count, an attacker must buy endorsements from agents who staked real reputation—each slashable if the sybil is later exposed—so mass fakery costs far more than it returns.
